(1) THE CLOCK IS TRANSPORT, NOT DOCUMENT: company/interfaces/wall_protocol.py::FRAME_WIRE_FIELDS gains `handed_over_at`, read by company/interfaces/wall_protocol.py::decode_frame_hand_over. It is a fourth REQUIRED frame key -- absence is never agreement here either, and the existing parametrised missing-field test covers it automatically because it parametrises over the constant rather than a hand-listed set. `observed_at` inside the envelope is when the counterparty says the FACT happened; this is when it says it PASSED IT ON, which is what a real Bacs transmission header carries and its transaction dates do not. (2) THE STAND-IN MUST STATE IT: simulation/payment_seam_adapter.py::frame_wire_message takes `handed_over_at` as a REQUIRED keyword with no default -- a default of `observed_at` would have made a prompt hand-over unfalsifiable by construction (the field could then never disagree with the document), which is the R15 TAUTOLOGY shape in miniature. A well-behaved bureau hands over promptly, so simulation/payment_seam_adapter.py::emit_wire_responses stamps each message's own `observed_at`; that is what makes the ordinary delivery the NULL CONTROL rather than an arbitrary threshold. SpecViolation.BACKLOG_BURST now stamps every message in the released queue with ONE instant, the latest, while each keeps its original `observed_at` -- the counterparty ADMITTING the delay in the only field that could carry it. (3) THE COMPANY TAKES DELIVERY AS A DELIVERY: company/billing/payment_observation_consumer.py::HandOverAssessment and company/billing/payment_observation_consumer.py::PaymentObservationConsumer.observe_hand_over, because a burst is a property of the SET and `observe_wire` sees one message at a time -- a per-message reader can no more detect a burst than a per-word reader can detect a sentence. company/billing/payment_observation_consumer.py::BUREAU_PROMPTNESS is one working day, sized from the Bacs cycle's daily reporting rather than tuned, and is a DIAGNOSTIC in the R12 sense: it decides what gets NAMED, never what the company believes. NOT A TAUTOLOGY, and this is the load-bearing design decision rather than a caveat. `handed_over_at` is the counterparty's CLAIM, and a claim checked only against other fields of the same message is checked against its author. So `observe_hand_over` takes `received_at` as a REQUIRED argument from the company's own clock and never reads it off the wire -- the same discipline pass 42 used for `supplied_accounts`. That is what lets HandOverAssessment.understated_delay contradict a counterparty that stamps a prompt hand-over on a message it actually sat on: the one fact it cannot author is when the bytes turned up. It is NOT defaulted to `utcnow()`, because a default would read the wall clock of whichever process ran and report a replayed 2026 batch as a year stale.
